title: Ravage Dungeons of Plunder - Review
body:
https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=bHJfRtPpY6E

Daniel (@dungeondive) reviews Ravage: Dungeons of Plunder, a Kickstarter he skipped during the campaign and bought later on the strength of praise in his Facebook group. He likes a good deal about the box. The cards have a linen finish, the table is unusually colourful for a genre that favours grime, the custom dice feel right, and the standees carry good art. He would take a well-drawn standee over an unpainted mini every time, and he has tubs of unpainted minis to prove it.

The premise promises a reverse dungeon crawl in which you play orcs defending your home, but in practice you are orc heroes doing everything any crawler does, with the adventurers recast as elite monsters and bosses. That would be fine. The rulebook is not. Nine pages of main rules and an alphabetised appendix manage to omit whether movement is diagonal, whether skill cards count as actions, and how you leave the dungeon, which matters because the first tutorial quest is to collect the treasure and escape. Every answer lives in a BoardGameGeek thread from the designer.

Daniel also questions the energy economy, where a card costing half your maximum energy buys a single die that the weakest monsters block routinely, and notes XP trackers too large for their slots. He gives the game a big pass, will not keep it, and holds out hope for a second edition.

----

How much can a BoardGameGeek errata thread rescue a game? Or is a rulebook that cannot explain its own tutorial quest a dealbreaker regardless of what else is in the box?
